phases.title: Screen-contextual demo triggers
phases.goal: Build one shared, pure trigger registry in src/shared, modelled on demoClockShortcuts, plus a small useDemoTriggerContext publish hook for screen state the URL cannot carry (edit draft, selected row, local tab), set on mount and cleared on unmount. Each entry declares route patterns, the surfaces it shows on (harness bar, PWA sheet or both), a run(api, ctx) that acts on the entity in the URL or the published context, and a disabled state. The harness bar gains one 'Demo actions' pill listing only the triggers for the current screen; the PWA gets the same list as a badged demo-actions sheet. Every existing Control Panel trigger is re-homed onto its screen, the Control Panel becomes the index (scenario jumps, clock and reset stay there), and the HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges plus an S1 caveat.
phases.delivers: A route-scoped 'Demo actions' menu in the harness bar and a PWA demo-actions sheet, with every existing Control Panel trigger re-homed to its screen, a context hook, 'Office authorises this List' on the PWA, and interim Future-scope badges
demo_triggers: Admin Audit: 'Simulate sign-in attempts' (an Admin sign-in with MFA, a failed attempt, an anaesthetist self-service password reset)
Admin Billing monitor: 'Trigger billing failure', 'Arm handoff failure', 'Run payables', 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed from the Control Panel)
Admin Review, on Dr Sharma's Tue 14 Jul List: 'Stage post-op scenario' (re-homed)
Admin Integrations, Surgeon PDFs tab (read through the context hook): 'Ingest PDF row' (re-homed)
Admin invoice document and Xero pair detail: 'Payment received (webhook)' Full or Half, and 'Replay last event', for the invoice in the URL (re-homed)
Xero sim: 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed)
Integrations simulator, Admin Integrations and mobile Lists: 'Fire hospital message' and 'Replay last (dedupe)', badged Future scope (re-homed; S1 fires it from the mobile screen)
PWA sheet, mobile List: 'Office authorises this List' (so 'Play the office' can default OFF, badged when on)
PWA sheet, mobile Balances: 'Payment received' Full or Half on an open invoice
phases.risks: pwaPurity.test forbids shell or demo imports in the PWA closure, so the registry, the context hook, trigger bodies and shared OFFICE and SOUTER actor constants live in src/shared or src/store. The 48px bar has no responsive handling: one menu pill, not many buttons. Office stand-ins declare the PWA surface only, because in the framed build the presenter plays the office in Admin. Playwright data-shot hooks (control-payment-webhook, control-scheduled-jobs, control-integration-message) move with their triggers, so the specs change here. Re-home first and re-green, then add the new pieces.
phases.goal_short: Build one shared, pure trigger registry in src/shared/demoTriggers (its own index, modelled on demoClockShortcuts, not re-exported from the shared component barrel), plus a small useDemoTriggerContext hook for screen state the URL cannot carry, such as the Admin Integrations tab and the simulator's selected message. Each entry declares its route patterns, where it shows (harness bar, PWA sheet or both), a run(api, ctx) that acts on the entity in the URL or on the published state, a disabled reason, and an index link with an optional hint. The harness bar gets one 'Demo actions' pill that lists only the current screen's triggers and is hidden when there are none. The PWA gets the same list as a badged bottom sheet. Every Control Panel trigger moves to its own screen, except 'Run payables', whose home is the Billing monitor's existing product button. The Control Panel becomes the index, keeping scenario jumps, clock and reset. FT-13.5 gets a 'Simulate sign-in attempts' trigger on Admin Audit that writes five audit rows. 'Play the office' is off by default, badged when on, and replaced in the story by a per-List 'Office authorises this List'. The HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges, and S1 gets a caveat.
checks: The harness bar shows no 'Demo actions' pill on the Admin Day view. On the Billing monitor it lists exactly four entries. Every Control Panel 'Open screen' link, with its hint where shown, lands on a screen whose menu contains that entry, and no trigger buttons remain on the Control Panel.

Make the RVG master editable with AA-sourced codes and their base units, and add AA-defined RVG groups (many-to-many tags) for Phase 26's prepaid tick list. Align the modifier master to the catalogue set with editable units and selection rules: add VM1, TTE1/2, PACU1, EAA1, POC1 to 3 and NC1/2, and retire PO1/PO2 (seeded Bookings are remapped). Anaesthetists (mobile and web) and the office choose it from a picker filtered by hospital, surgeon, insurer, funding source and RVG code. Insurer and funding source move onto the Booking (owner decision D2). Until Phase 21 stores a billable party, the payer is the selected Contract's holder, and the seeded funderOverride two-funder split stays as the split mechanism until Phase 22 replaces it. An anaesthetist's Contract change is recorded and flagged for office approval. Until Phase 27 derives it, prepayment becomes an office-set flag on the Booking.

phases.title: Billable party, required inputs and completeness
phases.goal: The Booking gains a billable party, defaulted from the Contract holder and overridable independently of pricing (guardian, hospital, another organisation, an insured patient who forwards the invoice), and invoices group by it, replacing the interim holder-as-payer. Each Contract declares the Booking inputs it requires (invoice email, billable party, prepaid amount, member number, claim reference, purchase order) and the Booking holds them. A Booking cannot be marked complete without a Contract, those inputs, and times on every timed Procedure. Patient-direct billing needs an invoice email, defaulted from the patient's own and capturable for a guardian. A 'procedure not on the Contract's schedule' flag replaces the silent BTM fallback. Office Review shows and approves every Procedure's Contract, shows the anaesthetist-change flag, and flags a child billable party at setup and review, blocking authorise of that List until an adult is set (owner decision D4).
phases.delivers: Billable party on the Booking with an independent override and grouping. Contracts declare required inputs; completion needs them. Invoice email for patient-direct. A not-on-schedule flag. Review approves every Contract and flags a child payer
demo_triggers: Admin Review: 'Stage child billed directly' (a spare SUBMITTED List, not the S2 or S3 Lists, with an under-18 billable party)
PWA sheet, mobile Booking: 'Office approves this Contract change' (clears the flag, audited as the office)
phases.risks: Billable party first, re-greened, then required inputs. The completion rules could block seeded Lists that S2, S3 and S4 use, so seed every required input on scripted Bookings. This supersedes the 8th-review ruling on the silent BTM fallback; record it in the Decisions log. The child block applies only to the staged List, so S2 Beat 4 stays non-blocking. US-08.2.1 is Verify; US-11.4.2 is Proposed.
phases.goal_short: Each Booking gets a billable party, meaning who receives the invoice. It defaults from each Procedure's Contract holder, or from the patient on the patient-direct RVG Default Post-paid Contract. The office or the anaesthetist can override it without changing the price, for example to a guardian, a hospital or another organisation. The billing run then raises one invoice per distinct party, which replaces Phase 20's interim rule that the payer is the Contract holder. A patient-direct Booking needs an invoice email, defaulted from the patient's or guardian's own and snapshotted on the invoice. Contracts declare the inputs each Booking must hold: invoice email, billable party, prepaid amount, member number, claim reference and purchase order. Mark complete needs a Contract on every Procedure, times on every Procedure and every declared input. A fixed-schedule Contract with no line for the code no longer prices silently by BTM. The Procedure is flagged 'to confirm with the hospital', only the office can set that Contract, and the office resolves it either with default RVG pricing and an explicit choice of who is invoiced, or by adding a new schedule line. Office Review shows every Procedure's Contract with Approve or Correct, plus who is invoiced with their email and address, the insurer line, and neutral flags for no Contract or an insurer still to add. It also flags a child billable party. Under D4's provisional default, a child payer or an open schedule miss blocks authorising the List. These are the only two blockers, and both come from one pure function.
checks: Hospital override: a Booking on the RVG Default Post-paid Contract, reassigned to Christchurch Eye, has an unchanged fee (to the cent) and one invoice to the hospital. S3's figures stay at $396.18, $152.38 and $91.43. The AIA Booking bills the patient and carries the note to claim from the insurer.

Mark complete refuses a Booking with no Contract, with times missing on any Procedure, or with a missing declared input or invoice email. sequencing_rules:
Before Phase 14: ask the owner for decisions D1 to D11 (table at the top of ROADMAP.md). D1 fee netting and basis (16), D2 insurer and funding source on Booking vs Patient (20), D3 ranged base-code bound (19), D4 child payer block or warn (21), D5 prepayment completion gate (27), D6 who raises the prepayment invoice at setup (27), D7 swap without office confirmation (32), D8 ageing and Overdue (38), D9 billed Lists vanish or stay (38), D10 additional-invoice pricing (39), D11 Booking without NHI (40). Each has a default reading; a phase whose answer has not come in builds the default and labels it provisional, and its drift check confirms the gating answer first. For 27, both branches of D5 are specified: by default the gate and its override go and the escalating alert is the control; if the gate is kept, it stays but fires from the derived requirement.

Order. Run 14 and 15 first, in either order; 15 before any phase that edits booking code (if 14 runs first, 15's rename covers the registry's patterns and labels). 16 straight after both, with fee removal re-greened as step 1 before the fee invoice. The Contracts track runs strictly in order, 17 to 25: 18 keeps today's resolver; 19 (RVG and Procedure masters) comes straight after 18 so base-unit sources are final before 23's Booking-level engine and 25's lock; 20 leaves two interims (payer is the Contract holder until 21 stores a billable party; funderOverride stays the split until 22's covered amount); 25 locks what 18 to 24 built, including 24's adjustment. 26 and 27 run back to back after 25; 20's office-set prepayment flag is the interim until 27. The Schedule track runs strictly in order, 28 to 32; 31 and 32 reuse 17's blacklist helper. Intake 33 to 35 runs after 31 and 20; 35 also needs 25. 36 runs after 16, 22, 25 and 27; then 37, 38 and 39 in any order. 40 after 34 and 36; 41 after 27 and 39; 42 after every master-data phase; 43 after 42; 44 last.
